common.style_usage: Stardew Valley building pixel art: palette, outline weight, how the roofs are shaded in rows of tiles or shingles with light ridges, dark gable edges and deep shadow under the eaves, and the high top-down front camera where the roof fills over half the building
common.reference_usage: camera, silhouette and roof planes: the lighter roof colour is roof facing up toward the viewer, the darker is roof facing forward, the darkest band is the shadow under the eaves; keep this outline, these openings, and the roof taking more than half the height

pottery_s2.description: A country potter's workshop in Stardew Valley pixel art: a terracotta clay-tile roof in rows with light ridges, a tall round red-brick kiln chimney on the right side, grey fieldstone walls, an open-fronted workshop bay with wooden shelves of bowls, jugs and vases, a small wooden door and window on the left, stacked firewood, a few pots drying outside. STRICTLY FRONT-FACING like every Stardew Valley building: the front wall seen square-on and flat, no side walls visible, not turned or rotated, no three-quarter or isometric angle; the roof seen from above and in front. Seen from above and in front like the Stardew Valley town buildings, a steep front-gabled roof whose ridge runs back away from the viewer, two big shingled roof planes (lit on the left, shaded on the right) filling about 60% of the height. Building only, nothing around it, no ground, no text, transparent background.
